items.followUp: What is meant by bus topology?

rubric.why: A central hub or switch is the defining feature of a star topology.
rubric.description: Names the central device to which the network is connected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a hub or switch as the central device.

rubric.why: The devices connect to the central device, not in a chain or ring.
rubric.description: States that every device is connected to the central device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing this connection arrangement.

rubric.why: In a star topology, each device has its own link to the central device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each device has a separate link.

rubric.why: Communication between devices passes through the hub or switch.
rubric.description: Explains the central device's role in communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that devices communicate through the central device.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, all computers and other devices are connected to one central device, such as a hub or switch.
Each device has a separate point-to-point connection to the central device.
Devices communicate with one another through this central device.

items.followUp: Describe how a switch forwards data in a star topology.

rubric.why: Data from a device is first sent to the central device.
rubric.description: States that the sending device sends data to the hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central device as the first destination for the data.

rubric.why: The central device receives and passes the data onward.
rubric.description: Explains that the central device forwards or sends the data onward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing onward transmission by the central device.

accept: hub sends the data to all connected devices
switch forwards it to the intended device
rubric.why: A hub and a switch handle onward transmission differently.
rubric.description: Describes broadcasting by a hub or forwarding to the intended device by a switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct description.

accept: accepts the data addressed to it
rubric.why: The intended recipient accepts the data sent to it.
rubric.description: Identifies what happens at the receiving device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the intended receiving device accepts the data.

modelAnswer: The sending device sends data to the central hub or switch.
The hub sends the data to all connected devices; a switch forwards it to the intended device.
The receiving device accepts the data addressed to it.
If the central device fails, communication across the network is disrupted.

items.followUp: Explain the problem-solving strategy called “work backwards.”

rubric.why: Acting out represents a problem situation by performing or modelling it.
rubric.description: Explains that “act it out” involves physically performing or role-playing the situation, or using a physical model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how the method represents the situation.

rubric.why: Following the actions and observing their results can help reveal a solution.
rubric.description: Explains how acting out helps solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the steps or actions are followed and their results observed.

modelAnswer: “Act it out” is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation is physically performed or role-played.
Following the steps and observing what happens can help reveal the solution.
